analysis:
This batch changes only CHANGELOG.md. Release preparation renames the v0.10.3 candidate to published and adds the v0.10.4 candidate notes (head 11-171). No source or threat-model text is in this batch, so no code-level regression can be established. The notes describe behavior whose implementation must be verified elsewhere:
(1) Periodic re-registration of unauthorized connections, which starts new coordinator verification sessions (TB-011, T-053, T-057). It must not let stale grants survive or let proofs be replayed across sessions.
(2) Delta complete checkpoints on the SSD prefix cache (T-041). Deltas must keep the HMAC naming, AAD binding, salt scoping, TTL and per-build namespace. The 0.10.3 reader refuses delta files.
(3) DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS is forwarded to the launchd job. Forwarded environment settings are an operator-controlled surface under TB-003.
(4) Add-on hold hardening: the signer is checked before a slot is taken, a 10-second line deadline applies, FIFO paths are refused and a model-load fence is added. These match the documented TB-012, T-059 and T-060 updates.
(5) A 30-second handshake timeout for the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002 availability).
(6) stop, restart and start now drain without coordinator acknowledgement when there is no session and no unfinished work.
(7) Grammar-constrained Qwen JSON and forced tool_choice advertisement (the T-007 output-integrity context).
(8) A Traffic status line and a coordinator_connection record in the daemon state file. These are local diagnostics; check that they carry no tokens or identities (T-058).
(9) Desktop auto-update feed and DMG signing. This is a new update-channel surface that the notes place outside the provider artifact; integrity of the feed and its signature verification was not reviewed here.
Changelog prose is untrusted evidence and does not prove these behaviors. The integration pass should confirm that the related source batches implement these controls.
